title: Danas u Travniku
theme: Day trip to Travnik in the present
reviewerNotes: This full draft is ready for human review before publication.
storyBeat: Ana and Emir walk Travnik and name what they see while Amira calls from the café.

vocabulary: Name mosques, towers, streets, and views with vidim, ovo je, and tamo je.
Use šetamo and Travnik landmark words in present-tense sightseeing talk.
grammar: Point and name with vidim and ovo je.
Place distant sights with tamo je and move with šetamo.
culture: Visit Travnik as a historic vizier town with colorful Sulejmanija Mosque.
Walk the old town and describe what you see in short present lines.

vocabulary.english: there is or it is there

grammar.title: Vidim and ovo je for what you see
grammar.explanation: Treat this as a ready chunk you can say today. Vidim means I see. Ovo je means this is. Point at a building and name it in one short present-tense line.

grammar.title: Tamo je and šetamo for place talk
grammar.explanation: Learn the usable chunk first. Full tables can wait. Tamo je points to something farther away. Šetamo means we walk. Use both chunks while you move through a town in the present.

grammar.title: Naming landmarks in the present
grammar.explanation: Take this as a speaking chunk. Do not memorize a case chart yet. Combine vidim, ovo je, and tamo je with džamija, kula, and grad. Keep every sightseeing line in the present tense.

culture.title: Travnik as a vizier town with colorful mosque
culture.body: Travnik was once the seat of Ottoman viziers in central Bosnia and Herzegovina. The old town climbs a hillside above the Plava Voda spring and keeps narrow streets full of color. Sulejmanija Mosque stands with painted details that travelers photograph from every angle. Ana and Emir walk the stone lanes and name what they see in short present-tense lines. A vizier town feels like a living museum where every corner offers a new view. Travnik rewards slow walking and polite greetings with locals.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson A. Point and name what you see
lessonBlocks.body: Start with vidim and ovo je. Point at Sulejmanija and say Ovo je Sulejmanija. Add džamija, kula, and stari grad as landmark nouns you can name today. Practice Vidim džamiju and Ovo je stari grad while you stand on a real or imagined corner. Ana walks beside Emir and tests each chunk before she takes a photo. Keep every sentence in the present tense. Sightseeing works best when you say the whole line together rather than hunting for a case ending.
tips: Point at a photo while you say ovo je.
Keep vidim and the landmark in one short line.
Stay in present tense for every sightseeing sentence.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson B. Walk the old town together
lessonBlocks.body: Move with tamo je and šetamo. Say Tamo je kula when the tower sits uphill. Invite a friend with Hajde da šetamo kroz grad. Amira joins by phone and asks what Ana sees right now. A passerby in Travnik points toward the old walls with a short polite answer. Mix ulica and pogled when you describe the walk. End with one postcard line that names Travnik as a vizier town.
tips: Use tamo je when the sight sits farther uphill.
Invite a friend with Hajde da šetamo.
Add molim or hvala when a passerby helps you.

conversation.title: Šetnja kroz Travnik
conversation.setting: Ana and Emir walk Travnik's old town while Amira listens on the phone and a passerby points the way.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.bosnian: Ovo je Sulejmanija. Vidim lijepu džamiju.
lines.english: This is Sulejmanija. I see a beautiful mosque.

lines.speaker: Emir
lines.bosnian: Da. Tamo je kula iznad grada.
lines.english: Yes. There is a tower above the town.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.english: Hello? What do you see now?

lines.speaker: Passerby
lines.bosnian: Stari grad je blizu. Šetajte pravo.
lines.english: The old town is nearby. Walk straight.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.english: Thank you! We walk through a narrow street.

lines.speaker: Emir
lines.bosnian: Pogled je prekrasan. Ovo je grad vizira.
lines.english: The view is wonderful. This is a vizier town.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.english: Send me a card from Travnik.

funFacts.title: Travnik was a vizier seat
funFacts.body: Ottoman viziers once governed from Travnik in central Bosnia and Herzegovina. The town keeps that history in its old walls and titles. Learners hear vizir as a cultural keyword rather than a grammar item.

funFacts.title: Sulejmanija stands out for color
funFacts.body: Sulejmanija Mosque is famous for painted details that catch the eye on a hillside walk. Ana names it with ovo je before she takes a photo. Colorful mosques make present-tense sightseeing memorable.

funFacts.title: Ovo je works like a pointing finger
funFacts.body: Ovo je plus a landmark is the fastest way to name what stands in front of you. You do not need a full case chart to start a Travnik walk. Point, name, and keep moving.

funFacts.title: Mountain roads need careful driving
funFacts.body: Roads into towns like Travnik often wind through hills. Fast driving on curves raises accident risk across the country. Travelers notice guardrails and tight turns on the way in.

questions.question: Why do traffic death rates stay high on many Bosnian roads?
options: Winding mountain routes combine with fast and risky driving
All highways are finished and fully lit
Cars are banned from mountain roads
Speed limits are enforced on every curve
questions.explanation: Sharp mountain roads plus fast driving help keep traffic deaths among the highest in Europe.

civicContext.title: Winding roads and fast driving keep traffic deaths high
civicContext.body: Road travel in Bosnia and Herzegovina remains far more dangerous than the European average. Mountain corridors use tight curves, mixed truck traffic, and limited overtaking space. High speeds among young drivers on those routes raise crash risk further. WHO country profiles still place the national traffic death rate among the worst in Europe, so a day trip can sit on infrastructure that has not caught up with safety needs.
